## About CopilotKit

[**CopilotKit**](https://www.copilotkit.ai) is an open-source framework for building AI copilots and agents into apps, with React components, in-app chat, shared state between the agent and the UI, and Generative UI. It also created **AG-UI**, an open protocol that connects agent backends such as LangGraph, CrewAI, and Mastra to the frontend. The main repo has more than [38K GitHub stars](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit).

Developers decide whether to use a framework like this by building with it. A feature list doesn't convince them; a complete app they can clone and run does.

## The challenge

CopilotKit's DevRel team already published on DEV. They needed more tutorials that:

* Build **complete apps** developers would want, not toy snippets
* Show new releases such as **CoAgents, LangGraph support, CrewAI support, and MCP** in a real project
* **Rank on Google** for the searches developers make when they start an AI app
* Keep bringing readers in **after the launch-day spike**

## Our role

Studio1 worked as an extension of CopilotKit's DevRel team:

* **Topic ideas and outlines**, each reviewed by the DevRel team before writing
* **Working demo apps** behind every tutorial, with GIFs and demo videos
* **Writing for search**, with titles and intros built around what developers type into Google
* **Distribution** on X, LinkedIn, and daily.dev, tagging the partner projects in each build
* **Docs feedback** from writers who built against new and pre-release features
* A **campaign** of posts, video, and a sponsor slot in [Awesome AI Apps](https://github.com/Arindam200/awesome-ai-apps)

## What we delivered

### 1. Five build-along tutorials on CopilotKit's DEV publication

Each tutorial builds one complete app with CopilotKit and the tools developers already use, from Cal.com and Google Maps to LangGraph, CrewAI, and Composio. All five are published under the [CopilotKit organisation on DEV](https://dev.to/copilotkit):

* [**How I Built the World's Best NextJS, AI Scheduling App**](https://dev.to/copilotkit/how-i-built-the-worlds-best-nextjs-ai-scheduling-app-442c) (October 2024): **9,881 views**, 42% from search
* [**Build an AI Travel Planner with CopilotKit, LangGraph & Google Maps API**](https://dev.to/copilotkit/build-an-ai-travel-planner-with-copilotkit-langgraph-google-maps-api-32fm) (January 2025): **9,036 views**, 27% from search
* [**Build an AI-Powered, Open-Source Notion**](https://dev.to/copilotkit/work-smarter-in-notion-add-a-copilot-with-copilotkit-50be) (February 2025): **2,323 views**, 24% from search
* [**End-to-End GitHub Workflow: Agents (CrewAI), UI (CopilotKit), Automation (Composio)**](https://dev.to/copilotkit/end-to-end-github-workflow-agents-crewai-ui-copilotkit-automation-composio-36aa) (July 2025): **1,638 views**, 9% from search
* [**Build a Multi-Agent Telecom Support System with CopilotKit & LangGraph JS**](https://dev.to/copilotkit/build-a-multi-agent-telecom-support-system-with-copilotkit-langgraph-js-52oc) (February 2026): **932 views**, 32% from search

Readers stayed. The travel planner, a 19-minute tutorial, has an **average read time of over 8.5 minutes** across 9K readers, and readers have saved the five tutorials to their DEV reading lists **470 times**.

### 2. Tutorials that rank #1 on Google

We picked each topic and title around a search developers already make, such as building an AI scheduling app in Next.js or an AI travel planner with LangGraph. Then we made the tutorial the most complete answer: working code, a demo, and every step to run it.

We checked Google on 18 November 2026 (US English, personalisation off). The tutorials rank:

* **#1** for "nextjs ai scheduling app", and the first source in the AI Overview
* **#1** for "ai travel planner langgraph google maps"
* **#1** for "open source notion ai copilot", above Notion's own AI page
* **#1** for "multi-agent telecom support system langgraph" on copilotkit.ai, and the first source in the AI Overview
* **#5** for "langgraph js multi-agent customer support"
* **#5** for "github workflow agents crewai composio", after Composio's own pages

Those rankings send readers every month. **7,557 views came from search engines**, 7,327 of them from Google, which is **32% of all tutorial views**. The scheduling tutorial alone has brought in **4,159 visits from search** since October 2024.

AI assistants have started sending readers too: **140 visits** came from ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude.

### 3. A demo app republished on the official CopilotKit blog

For the campaign, we built and open-sourced a [multi-agent telecom support system](https://github.com/studio1hq/support-help) with CopilotKit and LangGraph JS. Separate agents classify the request, look up the customer, reply or change their plan, and escalate to a human when needed. CopilotKit keeps the agents and the support UI in sync, so an agent can update a customer's service right in the app.

The tutorial went out on CopilotKit's DEV publication in February 2026. In April 2026, CopilotKit republished it on its [official blog](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/build-a-multi-agent-telecom-support-system-with-copilotkit-and-langgraph), where it now ranks #1 on Google for its search.

ChatGPT recommends it as well. Asked how to build a multi-agent telecom support system with LangGraph JS, ChatGPT (with web search on) lists the tutorial under "useful tutorials and resources", next to LangGraph's own documentation.

### 4. Distribution on X, LinkedIn, and daily.dev

We posted the tutorials on X and LinkedIn as they went live and tagged the other tools in each build, so their teams could share them too. For the GitHub workflow tutorial, CopilotKit gave CrewAI and Composio a heads-up before publishing so they could amplify it.

daily.dev sent **1K+ views** to the tutorials. Tracked links in our articles and posts recorded **4,200+ clicks to CopilotKit's GitHub repo** and 330+ to copilotkit.ai.

### 5. A campaign across posts, video, and Awesome AI Apps

From December 2025 to July 2026, we ran an organic campaign around CopilotKit's releases:

* **11 posts on X and LinkedIn** from Studio1's founders and creators, logged at **21.9K views**: the CopilotKit v1.50 release, CopilotKit trending on GitHub, AG-UI with Google ADK and TanStack AI, and Generative UI
* A YouTube video, [**Generative UI: The Secret Behind Adaptive Interfaces**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5aXNGtRQTY), on Generative UI and AG-UI with CopilotKit, plus a YouTube Short introducing CopilotKit
* A **sponsor slot** in [Awesome AI Apps](https://github.com/Arindam200/awesome-ai-apps), Studio1's open-source collection of 144 runnable LLM apps and agents, with **16.8K GitHub stars** and 1.9K forks

### 6. Feedback from building on new releases

Our writers often built on features before they were widely used: CoAgents, LangGraph support, CopilotKit's CrewAI support in the week of its March 2025 launch, and MCP. When a setup step failed or the docs and code disagreed, we sent the details to the DevRel team so they could raise it with the engineers.

## Why it worked

**We wrote for searches developers already make.** "Next.js AI scheduling app" and "AI travel planner with LangGraph" are what developers type when they start a project. A complete, working tutorial for that search can hold the top spot for years, as the 2024 scheduling tutorial shows.

**Every tutorial was a real app.** Readers got a scheduler, a travel planner, a Notion-style editor, a GitHub workflow, and a support desk they could clone and run. That kept them reading for minutes, saving the posts, and clicking through to the repo.

**Publishing on CopilotKit's own publication built its authority.** All five tutorials live under CopilotKit's DEV organisation, and the best one now lives on copilotkit.ai too. The rankings and AI Overview citations count for CopilotKit, not for a third-party blog.
